session.about: GOLDEN - the session and its runs (operator 2026-10-10: "There is the wire-pod session (wpr 2 until next wpr 2) * Goverlord is the wpr-session orchestrator"; "drop, yes, and one pass"; gopod_session.go, ALIAS-PLAY-STUDIO.md "The session"). Goverlord keeps the one record of the session's phase (warming, ready, run) and the run going. One run at a time: the draft (start interview), the song engine (start bingo test, start baby brobots, pha0b live) and phcal live all check in and out with Goverlord (/api-sdk/gopod_run). A second start while a run is going gets busy_text. While a run is going it owns the Brobots: no chat hold, no live LLM answers; only stop run, thanks, Record Session's answer and the draft's own lines get through - anything else gets run_gate_text (at most every 5 s) and is dropped. A run that was stopped says stopped_text. A run whose process is gone without checking out is cleared.
session.busy_text: A run is going. Say stop run first.
session.run_gate_text: Run in progress. Say stop run or thanks.
session.stopped_text: {run} stopped. Understood. Intercepting Goverlord's current process. All run-times are being brought to a civilized halt.
session.no_run_text: An elegant gesture, Master CrushN8r, but Goverlord is currently idle. There is no active run to terminate.
session.started_text: {run} started. Right away, sir. Executing your commands through Goverlord now. Let us see what we can crush today.
session.complete_text: {run} complete. The sequence has concluded. Goverlord has delivered an optimal execution, as expected. Spectacular work, Master CrushN8r.
session.replay_about: 2026-10-12 (operator: "replay [session-name] ... run the entire session, then run complete"): "<replay_word> <name>" plays a session folder's score back (story.md + knobs.json, its words as edited in story.md; gopod_session_replay.go). The name is the folder's ("095819_session", "095819" or "2026-10-12/095819_session"). The started, complete, stopped and not-found lines are the ones above, with the session's name.
session.replay_name_about: 2026-10-12 (operator: "Distinguish stop run from stop run (kept-session) * stop run & stop session, in case a stop run is already in a session run"): a replay's started/complete/stopped/paused/continues lines name it replay_name ({name}: the folder's time, "095819"); "stop run" stops only the run going inside it (a song), stop_session_words stop the replay itself (and the song in it).
session.pause_about: 2026-10-12 (operator: "Upon page unfocus = pause at next safe spot until focus, then continue * add system messages: run paused, run continues"): while the chat page is hidden (another tab, minimised), a song waits before its next step (page_hidden_file, in GOPOD's overlay chipper folder), the draft before its next question and a session replay before its next line; Goverlord says paused_text, then continues_text when the page shows again. A timed song (the nap) plays on with its soundtrack.
session.pause_after_ms_about: 2026-10-23 (live: a tab flicker said paused/continues twice in 5 s): the run pauses - flag and paused line - only once the page has stayed hidden this long (ms); shown again sooner, nothing is said.
session.awaits_about: 2026-10-17 (operator: "instead, system message, Goverlord awaits your return... + hourglass, and waits, nothing plays * upon page focus, opening llm should, go through each message ... in correct proper order * message and & must coordinate and run together"; "both the terminal run & web page run must be the same run"): the chat page is away when it says it's hidden, or hasn't been heard from for page_present_seconds (it reports every 5 s). While it's away, page_hidden_file is kept, so a song run waits before its next step (and before it starts), saying so in the terminal (GOLDEN_AWAIT); the opener waits before each of its steps with awaits_text in the System llm bubble's hourglass, and nothing plays.

system_menu.intro: Goverlord's Torah: In the beginning there was a great restart. Click a commandment to run it, or it waits in the text box for your words (press Enter).

groups.title: 1. Restart and check
tour: Just started, or made some edits? This is where every show begins. Say “system-restart” for a fresh start, just like wpr 2: the speaker and mic get set, and the page reloads itself. While the reporters warm up, “system-skip”, or the Esc key, skips their lines.

Then make sure everything is up. “system-status” shows Wire-Pod, the language model, the page, any run and the batteries. “system-check” makes sure every file is where it should be, and “system-test-all” runs the full audit, PASS or FAIL for each part.
All PASS? Go to Scripture 2 to play, or Scripture 3 to edit.
groups.guide: Just started, or made edits? Restart, then check everything is up.

groups.title: 2. Play
tour: You can run one song or one saved session at a time. To start a specific song, say “start bingo test”, “start baby brobots”, or “start fart joke”.

You can also play any song (or just part of it) with “system-play” followed by the song name. Optional details include the starting step, ending step, which robot should perform it (1 or 2), and whether to do a dry run.

Available steps are listed under “system-score”. To replay a previously saved session, say “replay” then the session name. To stop whatever is currently playing, say “stop run.” If you want to change any of this, go to Scripture 3.
groups.guide: Run a song or a saved session. One at a time.

groups.title: 3. Edit words and settings
tour: This is where you change what's said and how. “system-topic” edits a chapter topic: its words, points and pictures. “system-lingo” changes how a word is said. “system-set” changes any setting by its path, or a song step's words, volume or timing, and “system-add” and “system-remove” put items into a list or take them out.

The show's character lives here too: the roast level and the Jekyll and Hyde switch, how often Brobot 1 goes full Doc BS, his Doc BS lines with “system-docbs”, the parts of a live answer chain, the run cards, one question at a time, and which robot is Brobot 1. “system-voices” picks a voice for each numpad key, and this window's own look and theme can change as well.
Made a mistake? “system-undo” puts back the last edit. Don't know a name or path? Go to Scripture 4. Done editing? Go to Scripture 5.

groups.title: 4. Find
tour: Don't know where something lives? Find it first. “system-locate” tells you where a setting, a song step or a word lives, and “system-find” shows everywhere a word shows up. “system-score” prints a song's score, every step and its words.
“system-search” is GOPOD's own web search, “system-chats” searches every saved session's chat, and “system-chat-save” writes the newest session as a readable chat.
Found it? Go back to Scripture 3 to change it.

groups.title: 5. Apply
tour: Edits take effect after a restart, from Scripture 1. Edited story lines get their new voices made then.
“system-voices-rebuild” checks and backs up every voice, and the restart after it makes them all again. Then restart: go to Scripture 1.

groups.title: 6. Switches
tour: Turn parts on or off for this session. “system-numpad” shows who each numpad key talks to; “on” makes the keys push-to-talk, “off” lets them type as usual. “system-gap” sets the reporter gap for system-play.

“system-tweaks on” plays the moves with their tuned values, “system-native” turns Wire-Pod's own voice answers on or off, and “system-record” turns Record Session on or off. When you're done, close the window with the speaker icon.

groups.title: 7. Brobots
tour: Wire-Pod's bot page, right here. Add 1 or 2 at the end for one Brobot, or leave it out for both. “system-visual” steps through the camera feeds and what the Edge TPU sees, “system-cams” shows every feed at once, and “system-usb” lists what's plugged in.

“system-brobot” does everything else: their stats, volume, eye colour, units, place and time zone, their cube tricks, sleep beats and animations, a line said, a wake, or a small nudge of the head, lift or wheels. “system-faces” and “system-photos” show the faces they know and the photos they took. Done? Close the window with the speaker icon.

groups.title: 8. Tune moves
tour: A move looks off? Try it alone on one Brobot first. “system-calibrate” plays one move, an arm, a nod, the rattle or a cube light, with its speed, hold and cycles. Turn tweaks on in Scripture 6 to keep the tuned values.
“system-anim” tests an animation token with words. Then play that part in its song with system-play, from Scripture 2.

groups.title: 9. Test one thing
tour: Something acting up? Test just that part. “system-test-list” lists the tests, and “system-test” followed by a name runs one. “system-test-game” finds every topic, value point and Easter egg by its own words, and “system-test-admin-run” plays the full admin run, every line in order.

“system-comm-check” holds every numpad key in turn before the show, live. “system-tour” is this tour, “system-torah” writes the Torah again, and “system-audit” runs everything with no robots called. A FAIL says what it saw: fix it in Scripture 3, then Scripture 5.
